risks.note: Natural rubber, synthetic rubbers (PBR/SBR) and carbon black remain the dominant input cost variables and are subject to global supply and crude-linked price cycles. The escalation in West Asia in early 2026 further tightened global synthetic rubber and carbon black supply, with continued upside risk to crude flagged through FY 2026-27 and the rupee expected to depreciate to an average of around INR 94.5/USD over FY 2026-27 - both of which can pressure landed input costs. Managed through weekly price monitoring, calibrated pass-through and supplier diversification across geographies.

Geopolitical events in early 2026 affected synthetic rubber and carbon black availability and freight economics. Approximately 40% of India's natural rubber consumption and close to half of the tyre industry's synthetic rubber requirement are met through imports, making global trade dynamics, anti-dumping actions and shifting tariff regimes directly relevant to input costs even though the direct impact on the retreading segment is limited. Managed through vendor diversification, inventory discipline and production-vs-indent planning.
risks.risk: Logistics, supply chain and geopolitical risk

risks.note: The organised retreading market continues to see competitive activity from established players and new entrants. Volume risk is managed through the multi-tier premium/value portfolio, deep channel relationships and technical service, with management explicitly stating it meets competition with quality, consistency and partner economics rather than tactical discounting - implying margin exposure if it has to defend share on price.

The State Transport Undertaking business is subject to the variable cadence of government procurement, with revenue concentration tied to highly competitive, L1-driven public tender awards - an inherently lumpy, price-competitive channel that the Company can lose on any single tender cycle.
risks.risk: STU revenue concentration and public-procurement volatility

risks.note: Casing rejection rates for radial tyres are materially higher than for bias tyres, reflecting the lower repair-tolerance of steel-belted radial construction, and remain elevated industry-wide. Because M&HCV radialisation has already crossed 60% and is trending to 68-70% by FY30, this is a structural constraint on retreadable casing supply and is described as a near-term headwind for the retreading industry.
risks.risk: Radial casing quality and rejection rates

risks.note: As Millenium scales from its first commercial order to volume production in power electronics for BESS, execution risks around supply chain, working capital and customer development are actively monitored, with progress reviewed regularly at Board level. The adjacency is early-stage and unproven at volume.

The auditors drew attention to Note 46 on the valuation of the Company's investment in an oil exploration company in Nigeria: the fair value is subject to the successful exploration and production of hydrocarbon from the mining asset, and the outcome cannot be determined at present because exploration and production is on hold due to restrictions on flaring of gas by the Nigerian government. The auditor's opinion is not modified in respect of this matter.
risks.risk: Valuation of the investment in an oil exploration company in Nigeria (auditor Emphasis of Matter)

risks.note: EPR, GST and environmental regulations continue to evolve, requiring active monitoring and a structured compliance framework. Separately, treasury investments carry interest-rate and mark-to-market exposure, managed with a laddered maturity profile, conservative credit selection and avoidance of concentration in long-duration instruments. Management states that during the year no major risks were identified that, in the Board's opinion, threaten the existence of the Company.
